headline: BEARISH
headline_tag: Bitcoin holds near $60,000 after a month of losses

action.title: CUT / defend tightly with a stop-loss
action.detail: Keep acquisition running but defend it tightly: the headline is BEARISH, Bitcoin is about 25% lower than a month ago and holding just above $60,000, and a Fed rate rise on 8 December is widely expected. No Rally watch window is open, so there is no rally to chase and no fresh drop alarm either. Put every acquisition campaign on a 30-day return stop-loss and pause the ones that miss it, trim spend aimed at active traders (they tend to leave before conditions improve), and move messaging toward stablecoins, safety and education. Keep a reserve rather than cutting to zero; step acquisition back up only once price closes above the 200-week average ($68,220) and then the 200-day average ($71,820). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: Down about 25% over 30 days; Bitcoin is holding just above $60,000.
Price is about 18% under its 50-day average, 37 days in a row.
US spot Bitcoin funds lost about $487 million on the latest day.
watch: Fear is extreme, yet many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, so another slip could force those bets closed and make a drop sharper. A close above $62,750 and then $68,220 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the fall is easing; a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: the headline stays BEARISH; Bitcoin is holding just above $60,000 after a hard month, so today still calls for calm, safety-first messages and careful spending, not promotions. Short term, the picture is soft: Bitcoin, near $60,715, has closed under its 50-day average for 37 days in a row, sits about 18% below it and about 24% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 12 out of 100. Even so, many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which could make any further slip sharper, and about $7.6 billion of Bitcoin and Ether options expire on Friday (CoinDesk via PANews). A normal week lately swings about $4,069, so a close above $62,750 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; explainer and safety content fits better than offers.

The next month leans clearly down: price is about 25% lower than 30 days ago and about 22% lower than 90 days ago, and US spot Bitcoin funds saw about $487 million leave on the latest day. The Fed meets on 8 December, and markets put the chance of a rate rise there at about 98% earlier this week (CME FedWatch via PANews), which usually weighs on crypto around the meeting; a small plus is that Switzerland's first spot Bitcoin fund started trading (PANews). Bitcoin would have to win back $74,278 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. Keep bigger campaign pushes until after the Fed meeting and a clear turn.

Long term, the picture is flat rather than down: the 200-day average is still rising (about 4% over 90 days), but price is about 16% under it, about 11% under its 200-week average and about 51% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track while Bitcoin closes above $71,820 (the 200-day average); $68,220 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Slow structural steps continue on both sides, such as Israel Discount Bank adding Bitcoin trading to its app and Spain giving its anti-money-laundering agency power to freeze crypto accounts (both via PANews), but more weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and make keeping existing users the main use of budget.
